flags.note: Fact check, science passage: generally accurate. Imai et al. (House Foods, Japan), Nature 2002, identified LF synthase. In garlic the sulfenic acid self-condenses to allicin/thiosulfinates. LFS was silenced by RNAi in NZ (Eady, Crop & Food Research) with House Foods, around 2008; the result was much less LF and more thiosulfinates/zwiebelanes. Those onions were not commercialized. House Foods' tearless onion ('Smile Ball', around 2015) was made without GM. Its development has been reported to involve ion-beam/irradiation mutagenesis plus conventional breeding, so 'breeding ... without genetic engineering' is defensible but simplified. Its tearlessness reportedly comes from reduced alliinase activity, not from LFS suppression. The passage doesn't say otherwise, so it isn't an error. The kitchen-trick explanations are reasonable simplifications. One small point: 'For most of the twentieth century' is loose, because LF (propanethial S-oxide) was identified around 1971 and was then thought to form spontaneously. That still fits the 'alliinase-only' framing.

R058-01.notes: Revised account (alliinase-only -> LFS) plus what it enabled (tearless onion work, kitchen tips). A too argumentative; C off-topic; D covers only para 5.

R058-02.notes: Para 2: second enzyme converts intermediate into volatile irritant. A is alliinase's job; B is garlic self-reaction; C reverses.

R058-03.notes: 'The trouble was' signals an anomaly for the older account. B contradicted (alliinase works in garlic).

R058-04.notes: 'takes hold of' fits enzyme grabbing the intermediate. D 'attacks suddenly' is the tempting trap but too violent; B confiscates implies authority.

R058-05.notes: Para 3: intermediate might follow garlic-like path; para 4 confirms more flavor sulfur compounds. B misattributes to alliinase producing more; C contradicts.

R058-06.notes: Stated directly in para 4. D wrong country.

R058-07.notes: Sentence limits the tricks: they reduce formation/arrival but don't stop reaction. A too strong.

R058-08.notes: Sharp knife works by crushing fewer cells; fewer, cleaner cuts likewise damage fewer cells. A = chilling (slows enzymes), B and D = keeping irritant from arriving. Case for wrong options is weak; C is the only cell-damage option.

R058-09.notes: Defense against animals; effect on cooks incidental. A contradicts; B contradicts para 5.

flags.note: Option A is also the only one mentioning the opening events of para 1, and its wording ('Cutting breaks the cells') closely echoes the passage, so it's easy to pick. Still a valid detail question; no second defensible answer.

R058-10.notes: Cutting ruptures cells so alliinase meets sulfur compounds; precedes intermediate and LFS steps. B,D later steps; C last.

R058-11.notes: 'the light went thin' = dimming/faint at dusk. A/C are physical-width senses.

R058-12.notes: 'come out smaller than it was' = words would diminish its meaning. B contradicts 'I thought I knew'.

flags.note: 'looking back years later' is inferred rather than stated (the passage never gives the narrator's present age). The past tense and 'I was fourteen' support it well enough, and no other option is defensible.

R058-13.notes: First-person teen helper; past tense with 'I was fourteen' signals retrospection.
